name: search_inventory
description: Finds items by words (names, brands, serial numbers, text read from receipts and manuals) and by meaning ("something to make holes" finds a drill), best matches first, each with where it's kept; a box's 6-character QR label code finds the box. Start here whenever the person mentions a thing — to answer "where is…", and before create_item so you don't add a duplicate. For questions answered from documents ("what filter does the furnace take?") use ask_inventory; to browse a room, category or tag use list_items. Leaves out things that are gone or only wanted. Returns items, each with its id, fields, location path and what matched.

arguments.name: query
arguments.desc: What to look for, in the person's words: "drill", "something to make holes", a serial number or a box's label code

arguments.name: limit
arguments.desc: How many matches at most (optional)

name: ask_inventory
description: Answers a question in words from the household's own items and documents (receipts, manuals, warranty cards), citing the items it used — for "when does the dishwasher warranty end?" or "what filter does the furnace take?". Use search_inventory instead when the person wants to find a thing rather than learn a fact. Needs the server's AI to be switched on, counts as one AI action, and can take several seconds.

arguments.name: question
arguments.desc: The question, as the person asked it

name: get_item
description: Everything about one item: all its fields, where it's kept (and which box), warranties and claims, its photos and documents with what the vision model read in them, and any suggested fields waiting for the person to confirm. Use it after search_inventory or list_items has found the item, when you need the details; for what happened to it over time use item_history, and for a quick look at many items list_items is enough.

arguments.name: id
arguments.desc: The item's id, from search_inventory or list_items

name: list_items
description: Lists items, most recently changed first, 50 at a time (offset for more), with where each is kept. Use it to browse rather than search: with locationId, everything in that place and the places inside it ("what's in the garage?"); containerItemId, what's directly in a box; categoryId, a category and its subcategories; tag, a tag's items (a tag can be a collection, e.g. "Christmas decorations"); origin, how they were added ("claude": what you added, to check your own work); collectionId (list_collections), a collection's things — wanted "include" adds its want list, "only" just that. To find a particular thing by name, use search_inventory.

arguments.name: locationId
arguments.desc: Only what's in this place and the places inside it, from list_locations (optional)

arguments.name: containerItemId
arguments.desc: Only what's directly inside this box (an item with isContainer) (optional)

arguments.name: categoryId
arguments.desc: Only this category and its subcategories, from list_categories (optional)

arguments.name: tag
arguments.desc: Only items with this tag name (list_categories lists tags) (optional)

arguments.name: origin
arguments.desc: Only things added this way: app, photos, walkthrough, roomscan, scan, label, spreadsheet, homeassistant, claude, api (optional)

arguments.name: collectionId
arguments.desc: Only this collection's things, from list_collections (optional)

arguments.name: wanted
arguments.desc: The want list (things not owned yet): left out unless asked for (optional)

arguments.name: limit
arguments.desc: How many items in this page (optional)

arguments.name: offset
arguments.desc: How many to skip, for the next page (total says how many there are) (optional)

name: list_locations
description: Every property (home, cabin, storage unit…) with its locations as a tree (rooms › closets › shelves), their ids and how many items each holds. Call it to get a locationId or propertyId before create_item, move_item, list_items or create_location, and to check a place exists before adding it again. Read-only; the whole tree in one call.

name: what_needs_attention
description: What to act on now, urgent first: maintenance overdue or due within a week, warranties ending within 30 days, warranty claims with no news for two weeks, things running low, borrowed things due back, recalls that may affect something owned, insurance limits that fall short, and items or room scans from photos still to finish. Returns entries with kind, severity (urgent or soon), title, detail, the itemId to open (if any) and a date. Use it for "anything I should deal with?" or a daily check-in; for the full maintenance schedule use list_maintenance, for all warranties list_warranties, for what to buy shopping_list. Empty when nothing needs doing.

name: shopping_list
description: What to buy, run-out first: tracked consumables that have run out or are at or below their minimum (minQuantity, "keep at least"), with how many are left and a suggested amount to buy. Use it for "what do we need?" or before a shop; after buying, adjust_stock with a positive delta takes things off the list. Read-only.

name: item_history
description: What happened to one item, newest first: when it was added, each edit in words (moved from where to where, value, name…), photos and documents added, warranties and claims, maintenance done, stock used or restocked, loans. Use it for "when did we move the ladder?" or "when was the furnace last serviced?"; for the item as it is now use get_item. Get the id from search_inventory first. Returns entries with when (at), what happened in words, who, and how (the app, Claude, a script); more is true when there are older ones.

arguments.name: itemId
arguments.desc: The item's id, from search_inventory or list_items

arguments.name: limit
arguments.desc: How many entries at most, newest first (optional)

name: coverage_check
description: Checks the household's insurance limits against the inventory: each limit set in the app (contents cover, or a special limit on one category or tag such as jewelry or firearms) next to what those things are worth, how much short it is, and how many have no value recorded. Use it for "are we insured enough?"; for what everything is worth by room or property, use inventory_report. Limits are set in the app; amounts are in cents. Empty when no limits are set.

name: list_loans
description: Things lent out (who has them, since when, when they're due back) and things borrowed from others, still out, overdue ones marked, each with its loanId. Use it for "who has the ladder?" or "what have I lent out?", and to get the loanId for loan_returned. Only open loans; returned ones are in each item's item_history.

name: list_categories
description: The household's categories as a tree (ids, paths, item counts and any extra fields their items have — e.g. a TV's screen size), its tags with how many items carry each, and its item templates (kinds of thing with their own fields: a coin's year, mint mark and grade). Call it before create_item or update_item to pick a categoryId, existing tag names (to avoid near-duplicates) or a templateId — then put the template's or category's field values in customFields by their keys.

name: list_collections
description: The household's collections (coins, dolls, cards…): for each, how many things are owned (pieces counts duplicates), how many are on its want list, what the owned ones are worth and cost (cents), and its templateId (the fields its things have: list_categories). Use it for "how's the coin collection?" and to get a collectionId; the things themselves are list_items with collectionId.

name: list_warranties
description: Warranties on file across all items, soonest to end first. Returns each with its id, item, provider, start and end dates and status. Use it for "what's still under warranty?" or "what's about to run out?" (status expiring); for one item's warranties and claims use get_item, and for the urgent ones alongside everything else what_needs_attention.

arguments.name: status
arguments.desc: active: still covered (including expiring); expiring: ends within 60 days; expired. Left out: all (optional)

name: inventory_report
description: What everything is worth, for insurance: totals by property and by room, the most valuable items, and how many have no value recorded. An item counts at its value, else its purchase price, times its quantity; amounts in cents; gone and wanted things are left out. Use it for "what's all our stuff worth?"; to compare against insurance limits use coverage_check.

name: list_maintenance
description: Maintenance tasks (replace filters, service the boiler, clean gutters…), soonest due first, each with its id, the item or place and who usually does it. Use it to see the schedule, to get a task's id for complete_maintenance, and before add_maintenance so you don't add one twice; for just what's urgent across everything, what_needs_attention.

arguments.name: status
arguments.desc: open: everything not finished; overdue; due: within 14 days; upcoming: later; done: finished one-offs; all (optional)

arguments.name: itemId
arguments.desc: Only this item's tasks, from search_inventory (optional)

name: lookup_barcode
description: Says what product a UPC/EAN barcode is, and whether the household already has it. Use it when the person reads out or scans a barcode, before create_item; to find a thing by name use search_inventory. Looks in Ferret's own barcode book (learned from items saved on this server) first, then the online product database if it's switched on. Returns match (name, brand, model, source, photos — null when nobody knows the code) and youHave (the household's items with this code: id, name, quantity, place). When youHave isn't empty, offer adjust_stock on one of those rather than a duplicate, unless the person wants a separate item.

arguments.name: barcode
arguments.desc: The digits under the barcode (UPC-A, EAN-13 or EAN-8)

name: list_providers
description: The household's service providers (plumber, HVAC company, electrician…) with contact details, how many maintenance tasks they do, how often they've come, when they last did and what's been spent with them. Use it for "who did we use for the furnace?", to get a providerId for add_maintenance or complete_maintenance, and before add_provider so you don't add one twice.

name: recently_deleted
description: Items deleted in the last 30 days, newest first, with who deleted them and the day each goes for good. Use it when the person wants something back or asks what was removed; restore_item brings one back by its id. Only items — deleted maintenance tasks, places and the rest aren't listed.

name: room_scan_results
description: Checks on a room scan from scan_room (or one taken in the app): status pending (still looking — ask again in a little while), ready (what it found: name, category, how many — tell the person and ask which to keep), failed, or done (with the items it made). Without scanId, every scan still waiting to be finished. Once the person has chosen, add_from_room_scan adds them.

arguments.name: scanId
arguments.desc: The scan's id, from scan_room; left out: every unfinished scan (optional)

name: lend_item
description: Records that one of the household's items was lent to someone (direction "lent") or that something was borrowed from them ("borrowed"), optionally with a due-back date. Use it when the person says "I lent the drill to Sam"; get the item's id from search_inventory first. An item can have one open loan at a time; loan_returned closes it. Reminder emails to borrowers are set up in the app. Returns the loan with its id (for loan_returned) and due date.

arguments.name: itemId
arguments.desc: The item's id, from search_inventory

arguments.name: direction
arguments.desc: lent: the household's thing is with someone else; borrowed: someone else's thing is here

arguments.name: person
arguments.desc: Who has it (lent) or whose it is (borrowed)

arguments.name: since
arguments.desc: When it went (or came), yyyy-mm-dd; today if left out (optional)

arguments.name: dueOn
arguments.desc: When it's due back, yyyy-mm-dd (optional)

arguments.name: note
arguments.desc: Anything worth remembering about the loan (optional)

name: loan_returned
description: Closes a loan: a lent thing is back, or a borrowed one was given back. Use it when the person says so ("Sam returned the ladder"); the loanId comes from list_loans. The loan stays in the item's history and the borrower's reminder emails stop; nothing else about the item changes. Calling it again for the same loan is refused (it's already back).

arguments.name: loanId
arguments.desc: The loan's id, from list_loans

arguments.name: on
arguments.desc: The day it came back, yyyy-mm-dd; today if left out (optional)

name: add_photo
description: Attaches a photo — or a receipt, manual or warranty card as kind "document" — to an item that already exists. The vision model reads it in the background; about 20 seconds later get_item shows what it saw and any suggested fields: confirm them with the person before applying them with update_item. To add a new thing from its photo use add_item_from_photo instead. Counts as AI actions when the AI is on.

arguments.name: itemId
arguments.desc: The item's id, from search_inventory

arguments.name: kind
arguments.desc: photo: a picture of the thing; document: a receipt, manual or warranty card (photo or PDF) (optional)

arguments.name: data
arguments.desc: The image (or PDF, for a document) as base64; no data: prefix

arguments.name: filename
arguments.desc: The file's name, with its extension ("receipt.pdf") (optional)

name: scan_room
description: Finds the things worth inventorying in 1–5 photos of a room or an open box: the vision model lists each with a name, a category and how many. Use it when the person wants to add a lot at once; for one thing use add_item_from_photo. Say where with locationId (a room) or containerItemId (a box). It looks in the background: about 20–60 seconds later room_scan_results has the list. Nothing is added until add_from_room_scan, after the person has said which to keep. One AI action per photo.

arguments.name: photos
arguments.desc: 1–5 photos of the room or open box, each base64

arguments.name: locationId
arguments.desc: The room they show, from list_locations (optional)

arguments.name: containerItemId
arguments.desc: Or the box they show (an item with isContainer) (optional)

name: add_from_room_scan
description: Adds the things the person chose from a ready room scan (room_scan_results), as items in the scan's room or box — names can be corrected and a categoryId given. Only after the person has confirmed the list; the scan is then done, and each new item records that it came from a room scan. Returns the items made.

arguments.name: scanId
arguments.desc: The scan's id, from scan_room or room_scan_results

arguments.name: items
arguments.desc: Only the things the person chose to keep

name: add_item_from_photo
description: Creates a new item from a photo: it's saved straight away (as "New item" unless you give a name) with the photo attached, and the vision model reads it in the background. About 20 seconds later get_item shows its suggested name, brand, model and serial — confirm with the person, then apply with update_item. Use it when the person sends a picture of something to add; for a photo of something already in the inventory use add_photo. Put it somewhere with locationId or containerItemId.

arguments.name: data
arguments.desc: The image (or PDF, for a document) as base64; no data: prefix

arguments.name: filename
arguments.desc: The file's name, with its extension ("receipt.pdf") (optional)

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: Its name, if the person said it; otherwise it's "New item" until confirmed (optional)

arguments.name: locationId
arguments.desc: Where it's kept, from list_locations (optional)

arguments.name: containerItemId
arguments.desc: Or the box it's in (an item with isContainer) (optional)

name: file_warranty_claim
description: Records a claim made under one of an item's warranties: what went wrong, the provider's claim number (reference) and its status (filed by default, today by default). Use it when the person says they've contacted the maker or seller about a fault; get the warrantyId from get_item. Follow it up later with update_warranty_claim. Claims with no news for two weeks show in what_needs_attention.

arguments.name: filedOn
arguments.desc: When the claim was made, yyyy-mm-dd; today if left out (optional)

arguments.name: problem
arguments.desc: What went wrong, in the person's words

arguments.name: reference
arguments.desc: The provider's claim or case number (optional)

arguments.name: status
arguments.desc: Where it stands: filed, in_progress, approved, denied or resolved (optional)

arguments.name: resolution
arguments.desc: How it ended: repaired, replaced, refunded… (optional)

arguments.name: resolvedOn
arguments.desc: When it was closed, yyyy-mm-dd (optional)

arguments.name: costCents
arguments.desc: What the household paid out of pocket, in cents (optional)

arguments.name: notes
arguments.desc: Anything else: calls made, who said what (optional)

arguments.name: warrantyId
arguments.desc: The warranty's id, from get_item

name: update_warranty_claim
description: Changes a warranty claim: its status (filed, in_progress, approved, denied, resolved), the resolution, what it cost (cents), the claim number. Use it when the person hears back about a claim; the claim's id is in get_item. Closing it (denied or resolved) dates it today unless resolvedOn is given. Fields left out stay as they are.

arguments.name: filedOn
arguments.desc: When the claim was made, yyyy-mm-dd; today if left out (optional)

arguments.name: problem
arguments.desc: What went wrong, in the person's words (optional)

arguments.name: reference
arguments.desc: The provider's claim or case number (optional)

arguments.name: status
arguments.desc: Where it stands: filed, in_progress, approved, denied or resolved (optional)

arguments.name: resolution
arguments.desc: How it ended: repaired, replaced, refunded… (optional)

arguments.name: resolvedOn
arguments.desc: When it was closed, yyyy-mm-dd (optional)

arguments.name: costCents
arguments.desc: What the household paid out of pocket, in cents (optional)

arguments.name: notes
arguments.desc: Anything else: calls made, who said what (optional)

arguments.name: id
arguments.desc: The claim's id, from get_item

name: add_provider
description: Adds a service provider — a plumber, the HVAC company, an electrician — with their trade and contact details, so maintenance can name who does it. Check list_providers first so you don't add one twice; then use its id as providerId on add_maintenance or complete_maintenance. Returns the new provider with its id.

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: The business or person: "Acme Heating & Air"

arguments.name: trade
arguments.desc: What they do: "Plumber", "HVAC", "Appliance repair" (optional)

arguments.name: contactName
arguments.desc: Who to ask for (optional)

arguments.name: phone
arguments.desc: Phone number, as they give it (optional)

arguments.name: email
arguments.desc: Email address (optional)

arguments.name: website
arguments.desc: Their website (optional)

arguments.name: address
arguments.desc: Their business address (optional)

arguments.name: notes
arguments.desc: Anything worth remembering: rates, who to ask for, what they did well (optional)

name: create_item
description: Adds a new item. Search first (search_inventory) so you don't add a duplicate; if it's already there, update_item or adjust_stock instead. Put it somewhere with locationId (list_locations) or in a box with containerItemId, and give it a categoryId and tags (list_categories; new tag names are created). Prices in cents. For a collection, collectionId (list_collections) starts it from the collection's template; wanted: true puts it on the want list (looked for, not owned yet), and update_item with wanted: false once it's got. From a photo, use add_item_from_photo. Returns the new item with its id.

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: What it is, the way people would look for it: "Cordless drill"

arguments.name: description
arguments.desc: A longer description: colour, size, what it's for (optional)

arguments.name: brand
arguments.desc: Who made it (optional)

arguments.name: model
arguments.desc: Model name or number, as on its label (optional)

arguments.name: serialNumber
arguments.desc: Its serial number, for warranty claims and insurance (optional)

arguments.name: barcode
arguments.desc: Its UPC/EAN barcode (also learned into the household's barcode book) (optional)

arguments.name: quantity
arguments.desc: How many there are; to count stock up or down, adjust_stock logs the change (optional)

arguments.name: minQuantity
arguments.desc: Keep at least this many: at or below it, it goes on the shopping list (optional)

arguments.name: usageUnit
arguments.desc: What its counter measures, for maintenance by use (a car's miles, a mower's hours) (optional)

arguments.name: condition
arguments.desc: What shape it's in (optional)

arguments.name: purchaseDate
arguments.desc: When it was bought, yyyy-mm-dd (optional)

arguments.name: purchasePriceCents
arguments.desc: What was paid for one, in cents (12999 = $129.99) (optional)

arguments.name: valueCents
arguments.desc: What one is worth now, in cents — used for the insurance report (optional)

arguments.name: notes
arguments.desc: Anything else worth keeping: where the spare key is, quirks, settings (optional)

arguments.name: favorite
arguments.desc: Starred, to find quickly in the app (optional)

arguments.name: heir
arguments.desc: Who should have it one day (optional)

arguments.name: isContainer
arguments.desc: A box, bin or case that holds other items (they set containerItemId to it) (optional)

arguments.name: locationId
arguments.desc: Where it's kept: a location id from list_locations (null: nowhere in particular) (optional)

arguments.name: containerItemId
arguments.desc: The box it's in: an item id with isContainer; it's then wherever the box is (optional)

arguments.name: categoryId
arguments.desc: A category id from list_categories (optional)

arguments.name: tags
arguments.desc: Tag names; new ones are created. When updating, the full new list (optional)

arguments.name: customFields
arguments.desc: Values for its category's or template's extra fields, by their keys (list_categories shows them) (optional)

arguments.name: templateId
arguments.desc: The item template it's made from (list_categories), whose fields it then has (optional)

arguments.name: collectionId
arguments.desc: The collection it's part of (list_collections) (optional)

arguments.name: wanted
arguments.desc: On the want list: not owned yet — left out of totals, the report, stock and search unless asked for (optional)

arguments.name: links
arguments.desc: Web links: the maker's page, the manual online… When updating, the full new list (optional)

arguments.name: disposition
arguments.desc: No longer had: sold, given, discarded, lost or stolen (null: still have it). Gone items leave lists and totals (optional)

arguments.name: disposedOn
arguments.desc: When it went, yyyy-mm-dd (optional)

arguments.name: disposalCents
arguments.desc: What it sold for, in cents (optional)

arguments.name: disposalNote
arguments.desc: Who it went to, or what happened (for a lost or stolen claim) (optional)

arguments.name: origin
arguments.desc: Which of the app's ways added it; ignored for Claude and API keys (recorded by the server) (optional)

name: update_item
description: Changes some of an item's fields — name, brand, value, category, notes, the box it's in… — after the person has said what to change (or confirmed suggestions from get_item). Fields left out stay as they are; send null to clear one. `tags` and `links` replace the whole list (send the old ones you want to keep). For just moving it use move_item; for using some up or restocking use adjust_stock, which logs the change; for a counter reading use record_reading. Returns the updated item.

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: What it is, the way people would look for it: "Cordless drill" (optional)

arguments.name: description
arguments.desc: A longer description: colour, size, what it's for (optional)

arguments.name: brand
arguments.desc: Who made it (optional)

arguments.name: model
arguments.desc: Model name or number, as on its label (optional)

arguments.name: serialNumber
arguments.desc: Its serial number, for warranty claims and insurance (optional)

arguments.name: barcode
arguments.desc: Its UPC/EAN barcode (also learned into the household's barcode book) (optional)

arguments.name: quantity
arguments.desc: How many there are; to count stock up or down, adjust_stock logs the change (optional)

arguments.name: minQuantity
arguments.desc: Keep at least this many: at or below it, it goes on the shopping list (optional)

arguments.name: usageUnit
arguments.desc: What its counter measures, for maintenance by use (a car's miles, a mower's hours) (optional)

arguments.name: condition
arguments.desc: What shape it's in (optional)

arguments.name: purchaseDate
arguments.desc: When it was bought, yyyy-mm-dd (optional)

arguments.name: purchasePriceCents
arguments.desc: What was paid for one, in cents (12999 = $129.99) (optional)

arguments.name: valueCents
arguments.desc: What one is worth now, in cents — used for the insurance report (optional)

arguments.name: notes
arguments.desc: Anything else worth keeping: where the spare key is, quirks, settings (optional)

arguments.name: favorite
arguments.desc: Starred, to find quickly in the app (optional)

arguments.name: heir
arguments.desc: Who should have it one day (optional)

arguments.name: isContainer
arguments.desc: A box, bin or case that holds other items (they set containerItemId to it) (optional)

arguments.name: locationId
arguments.desc: Where it's kept: a location id from list_locations (null: nowhere in particular) (optional)

arguments.name: containerItemId
arguments.desc: The box it's in: an item id with isContainer; it's then wherever the box is (optional)

arguments.name: categoryId
arguments.desc: A category id from list_categories (optional)

arguments.name: tags
arguments.desc: Tag names; new ones are created. When updating, the full new list (optional)

arguments.name: customFields
arguments.desc: Values for its category's or template's extra fields, by their keys (list_categories shows them) (optional)

arguments.name: templateId
arguments.desc: The item template it's made from (list_categories), whose fields it then has (optional)

arguments.name: collectionId
arguments.desc: The collection it's part of (list_collections) (optional)

arguments.name: wanted
arguments.desc: On the want list: not owned yet — left out of totals, the report, stock and search unless asked for (optional)

arguments.name: links
arguments.desc: Web links: the maker's page, the manual online… When updating, the full new list (optional)

arguments.name: disposition
arguments.desc: No longer had: sold, given, discarded, lost or stolen (null: still have it). Gone items leave lists and totals (optional)

arguments.name: disposedOn
arguments.desc: When it went, yyyy-mm-dd (optional)

arguments.name: disposalCents
arguments.desc: What it sold for, in cents (optional)

arguments.name: disposalNote
arguments.desc: Who it went to, or what happened (for a lost or stolen claim) (optional)

arguments.name: id
arguments.desc: The item's id, from search_inventory or list_items

name: adjust_stock
description: Counts consumables up or down — filters, batteries, bulbs: negative delta for used up ("we used the last AA pack" → -1), positive for bought more. Use it whenever the person uses up or buys something tracked; it never goes below 0, logs the change in the item's stock history, and moves the item on or off the shopping list. To set an exact count (after a recount), use update_item's quantity. Returns the new count.

arguments.name: id
arguments.desc: The item's id, from search_inventory

arguments.name: delta
arguments.desc: How many used (negative) or bought (positive); not 0

arguments.name: note
arguments.desc: Why, for its stock history ("used for the guest room") (optional)

name: record_reading
description: Records what an item's counter says now — a car's odometer, a mower's or generator's engine hours, a furnace's run hours — in the item's usageUnit (set it with update_item first: miles, km, hours or cycles). Maintenance by use on that item ("every 5,000 miles") is rescheduled from it. Use it when the person mentions a reading; when they've just done the maintenance, give the reading to complete_maintenance instead.

arguments.name: value
arguments.desc: What the counter says now, in the item's usageUnit

arguments.name: readOn
arguments.desc: When it was read, yyyy-mm-dd; today if left out (optional)

arguments.name: note
arguments.desc: Anything worth noting with the reading (optional)

arguments.name: id
arguments.desc: The item's id (one with a usageUnit), from search_inventory

name: move_item
description: Records that an item now lives somewhere else: a location from list_locations, or null for nowhere in particular. Use it for "I put the drill in the basement"; moving a box takes what's inside it along, and moving something that was in a box takes it out of the box. To put something into a box, use update_item with containerItemId. The move shows in item_history.

arguments.name: id
arguments.desc: The item's id, from search_inventory

arguments.name: locationId
arguments.desc: Where it is now, from list_locations; null: nowhere in particular

name: delete_item
description: Removes an item from the inventory — only when it was added by mistake or the person wants it gone from the records. For something sold, given away, thrown out, lost or stolen, prefer update_item with disposition, which keeps it for insurance and history. It stays in Recently deleted for 30 days (restore_item brings it back), then goes for good with its photos and documents. Confirm with the person first.

arguments.name: id
arguments.desc: The item's id, from search_inventory

name: restore_item
description: Brings back an item from Recently deleted (ids from recently_deleted), with its photos, documents, warranties and maintenance. Use it when the person wants a deleted thing back within 30 days. If its place or box was removed meanwhile, it comes back without one — move_item can put it somewhere. Returns the restored item's id and name.

arguments.name: id
arguments.desc: The deleted item's id, from recently_deleted

name: create_property
description: Adds a property — a home, vacation home, rental, storage unit or vehicle — the top level of where things are kept. Only name is required (type defaults to home); the address is optional and only used for its map picture. Check list_locations first so you don't add one twice. Rooms, closets and shelves are locations inside it: add them next with create_location. Returns the new property with its id.

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: What the household calls it: "Home", "Lake cabin", "Storage unit 12"

arguments.name: type
arguments.desc: What kind of property it is (optional)

arguments.name: street
arguments.desc: Street address (used for its map picture, if maps are on) (optional)

arguments.name: city
arguments.desc: Town or city (optional)

arguments.name: region
arguments.desc: State, province or region (optional)

arguments.name: postalCode
arguments.desc: ZIP or postal code (optional)

arguments.name: country
arguments.desc: Country name (optional)

arguments.name: yearBuilt
arguments.desc: The year the building was built (optional)

arguments.name: valueCents
arguments.desc: What the property itself is worth, in cents (not its contents) (optional)

arguments.name: notes
arguments.desc: Anything else worth keeping about it (optional)

name: create_location
description: Adds a location — a room, closet or shelf — to a property, optionally inside another location (parentId), and optionally with locations inside it in one go: "a garage with three shelves" is name "Garage", children ["Shelf 1", "Shelf 2", "Shelf 3"]. Check list_locations first so you don't add one twice. propertyId can be left out when there's only one property; a new property itself is create_property. Returns the new locations with their ids.

arguments.name: propertyId
arguments.desc: The property, from list_locations; can be left out when there's only one (optional)

arguments.name: parentId
arguments.desc: The location it's inside (a shelf in a closet), from list_locations; null: directly in the property (optional)

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: What the household calls it: "Garage", "Hall closet", "Top shelf"

arguments.name: icon
arguments.desc: An icon name for the app (optional) (optional)

arguments.name: notes
arguments.desc: Anything else worth keeping about it (optional)

arguments.name: children
arguments.desc: Names of locations to make inside it in one go: ["Shelf 1", "Shelf 2"] (optional)

name: add_maintenance
description: Adds upkeep to track: on an item (itemId), a place (locationId) or the whole household. Give intervalCount + intervalUnit for something that repeats ("every 3 months"), or neither for a one-off. dueOn defaults to one interval from today (today for a one-off). By use ("every 5,000 miles"): usageEvery, on an item that counts something — set the item's usageUnit (update_item) and log a reading (record_reading) first; it can have a time interval too (whichever comes first). Check list_maintenance first so you don't add it twice. Due tasks show in what_needs_attention and the household's reminders.

arguments.name: title
arguments.desc: What to do: "Replace furnace filter", "Clean gutters"

arguments.name: notes
arguments.desc: How to do it: the part number, steps, what to watch for (optional)

arguments.name: itemId
arguments.desc: The item it's for (search_inventory); leave out for a place or the whole household (optional)

arguments.name: locationId
arguments.desc: The place it's for, e.g. "Clean gutters" on the roof (list_locations) (optional)

arguments.name: intervalCount
arguments.desc: Repeats every this many intervalUnits ("every 3 months": 3); leave both out for a one-off (optional)

arguments.name: intervalUnit
arguments.desc: The unit of intervalCount (optional)

arguments.name: dueOn
arguments.desc: When it's next due, yyyy-mm-dd; defaults to one interval from today (today for a one-off) (optional)

arguments.name: attachmentId
arguments.desc: The manual it came from: a document's id from get_item (optional)

arguments.name: providerId
arguments.desc: Who usually does it, from list_providers (optional)

arguments.name: partItemId
arguments.desc: The consumable it uses (a filter item): marking it done takes partQuantity out of stock (optional)

arguments.name: partQuantity
arguments.desc: How many of the part each time (default 1) (optional)

arguments.name: usageEvery
arguments.desc: Also (or only) due every this much use, in the item's usageUnit ("every 5,000 miles": 5000). Needs itemId (optional)

name: complete_maintenance
description: Records that a task was done (today, or doneOn), with an optional note and cost in cents — use it whenever the person says they did one ("changed the furnace filter"); the id comes from list_maintenance. Credited to the task's usual provider unless providerId says otherwise (null: the household did it), and its part, if it has one, comes out of stock. A repeating task is then due again one interval after that day; a one-off is finished. For maintenance by use, give reading (what the odometer or hour meter says now): the next is due usageEvery after it. Returns the task with its new due date.

arguments.name: doneOn
arguments.desc: When it was done, yyyy-mm-dd; today if left out. The next due date counts from this day (optional)

arguments.name: note
arguments.desc: Anything worth remembering about this time (optional)

arguments.name: costCents
arguments.desc: What it cost this time, in cents (optional)

arguments.name: providerId
arguments.desc: Who did it this time (list_providers); left out: the task's usual provider; null: the household (optional)

arguments.name: usePart
arguments.desc: Take the task's part out of stock (default true; false when an old one was cleaned instead) (optional)

arguments.name: reading
arguments.desc: Maintenance by use: what the item's counter says now; the next one is due usageEvery after it (optional)

arguments.name: id
arguments.desc: The task's id, from list_maintenance

name: delete_maintenance
description: Deletes a maintenance task the household no longer needs (the item is gone, or it was added by mistake), so it stops coming due and leaves reminders. This is not for a task that was just done — use complete_maintenance, which schedules the next one. The past times it was done stay in the item's history; the task itself can't be brought back with these tools. Confirm with the person first.

arguments.name: id
arguments.desc: The task's id, from list_maintenance
